gaps.sentence: ___, I'd like to thank the volunteers who worked behind the scenes.
gaps.explanation: 'Finally' introduces the last point of a list or speech.

gaps.sentence: Please complete the form in block capitals ___ it can be read easily.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces a clause with subject and modal; so as to/in order to need an infinitive.

gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
The expedition will go ahead ___ the sponsors confirm the funding.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' = only if, a formal positive condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ his impressive qualifications, he wasn't even shortlisted.
Take a map ___ you get lost in the backstreets.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against something that might happen.

gaps.sentence: He lowered his voice ___ wake the baby.
gaps.explanation: Negative purpose = so as not to / in order not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: She earns a very good salary; ___, she never seems to have any money.
gaps.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts two facts, like but, in a slightly more formal way.
